messages:
Ellen: Hi team I need to add my partner to medical and dependent life. We tied the knot in the US but their work visa renewal is delayed and we just received the marriage certificate. Missed the 30-day window by ~12 days. Can we file an exception?
Nadia (People Ops): Congrats, Ellen! :tada: Marriage is a QLE. Exceptions are possible for administrative delays like visa processing or delayed document receipt. We'll need a short packet to start.
Ellen: Great. What exactly do you need? The consulate paperwork and I-539 receipt both show processing delays. Partner also doesn't have an SSN yet due to the visa gap.
Samir (Benefits): Helpful docs: certified marriage certificate, passport bio page, visa/immigration receipts showing pending renewal, any correspondence from USCIS/consulate noting backlog, and a short cover note from you explaining dates. For SSN, carriers accept "SSN pending" plus passport/visa docs.
Nadia (People Ops): Action steps: 1) Upload marriage certificate (certified English translation if needed). 2) Upload I-539 or visa renewal receipt and any consulate emails. 3) Upload passport page. 4) Complete "Change Outside Open Enrollment" form on the benefits portal and choose "Exception - documentation/visa delay". 5) Email the portal confirmation and docs to benefits@redwood.com with subject: "BEN-EXCEPTION-1795678901".
Ellen: If exception is approved, will medical cover prescriptions from the date of the wedding? Partner is on a maintenance med.
Samir (Benefits): Carrier discretion. We'll request retroactive effective date to the marriage date given the medical need. If carrier approves retro effective date, eligible claims during that window may be reimbursable. We'll help submit retro claims if approved.
Ellen: Any naming convention to speed intake?
Nadia (People Ops): Yes: "Lastname_Firstname_docType_DATE.pdf" (e.g., Allen_Ricardo_visareceipt_2026-04-02.pdf). Also include the portal ticket number in the email body.
BenefitsBot: Submission received: Ticket BEN-1795678901 created. Intake team will assign to Benefits for review.
Nadia (People Ops): Timeline: we send to carrier same day we get the packet. Carrier response typically 5-14 business days. We'll ping once we have news.
Ellen: Thanks Uploading docs now. Appreciate the help.
Samir (Benefits): If carrier asks for additional proof (apostille, notarized translation), we'll let you know and provide templates. Hang tight.
